summary: Protected Coordination PR1000 adds six current supplier-wire-v1 response/context controls derived from existing context-response-genesis source. A preserves original response/context; B changes only challenge ID/nonce and recomputes the existing challenge-domain digest. Both matched pairs pass structural/context consistency only with synthetic opaque signatures and untrusted authority. Crossed A/B contexts and raw-SHA256/response-domain substitutions all preserve valid standalone envelope structure but refuse original-response-head-challenge. Exact bytes, SHA256, lengths, domain tables, mutation isolation and source hashes are checked by the documented pure qualifier controls; six vectors/six contexts pass with authentication=false/nativeAcceptance=false. Existing251-case corpus and31 sizing vectors are separate retained evidence; no production code/schema/wire/journal behavior changes. Current challenge rule remains SHA256(ASCII fsgg.v3.challenge/1 + NUL + exact challenge bytes). Companion raw-SHA proof challenge, shared pending typed ledger and persisted-reader compatibility remain undecided. No authenticated semantic positive, new signing role/wire version, durable replay behavior, native proof or operational identity follows; capabilities remain false and native campaign/original attempt remain null/unknown. The first same-head eligibility attempt failed a stale review marker; a later repaired eligibility run succeeded, so protected source acceptance is not an all-historical-runs-green claim. This shared record captures the cross-repository source boundary without private host findings.
title: V3 current-wire corpus separates untrusted context consistency from authenticated authority
